reproducibility_analysis: Fixed target classes and fixed +3m planned gap make coarse-ascent samples comparable.
Changing workload profile should be explicit and deliberate, not accidental.
Generated workload should have a predeclared or bounded extension rule to avoid both exhaustion and meaningless padding.
Immutable batch files provide proof of continued substantive work across the invocation.
Scheduler validation at start should remain identical across target classes.
Close evidence schema should remain stable enough for later aggregation.
Retrospective wake evidence should not rewrite prior immutable files; attach separately or summarize in state.
The same automation ID preserves the relay condition under study.
A recurring RRULE must remain present after each pre-arm update.
Target escalation should occur only from durable classification, never from expected elapsed time.
If future samples show provider drift, rerun nearby classes rather than assuming historical stability.
These controls improve the chance that the final operating contract generalizes beyond one lucky run.
